title: Trump Says Iran Deal Isn't Good Enough Yet — What's the Hold-Up?
summary: Imagine a giant game of tug-of-war, but instead of a rope, it's over a super important waterway called the Strait of Hormuz. That's where a lot of the world's oil travels through. Right now, the U.S. and Iran are in a tense standoff. President Trump said on Wednesday he's 'not satisfied' yet with the deal they're trying to make. He thinks Iran really wants an agreement, but he warned, 'so far they haven't gotten there.' If they don't reach a deal, Trump said the U.S. might have to 'just finish the job,' meaning more military strikes could happen. Earlier, Iranian TV reported details of a draft deal. It said the U.S. would lift its naval blockade (a kind of sea wall) of Iran's ports, and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz to normal ship traffic within a month. But the White House quickly called that report a 'complete fabrication' — a fancy way of saying it's totally made up. The conflict started in February when the U.S. and Israel launched big strikes on Iran. Iran fought back and blocked the strait, causing oil prices to shoot up worldwide. A ceasefire (when both sides agree to stop fighting for a while) was agreed on in April, but talks to make a lasting peace got stuck. Just this week, the U.S. launched new strikes in southern Iran, saying they were for self-defense. Iran said that broke the ceasefire. So, the world watches and waits. Will they finally agree, or will the fighting start again?
why_it_matters: If the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked, oil prices could rise, making gasoline and many things your family buys more expensive.

background_read: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. About one-fifth of the world's oil travels through it every day.
President Donald Trump (who became U.S. president again in 2025) has had a rocky relationship with Iran. In his first term, he pulled the U.S. out of a nuclear deal with Iran.
In early 2025, tensions erupted when the U.S. and Israel struck Iran, leading Iran to block the strait, which made oil prices jump around the world.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, Iranian TV, the White House, U.S. military
WHAT: Trump says he is 'not satisfied' with the deal; Iranian TV claims a draft deal exists; the White House calls that report a complete fabrication
WHERE: The Strait of Hormuz, between Iran and the U.S.
WHY: The conflict began in February with U.S.-Israel strikes; Iran blocked the strait; a ceasefire was reached in April but new strikes broke it again

perspectives.description: Iran is not serious about a lasting deal, and the U.S. may need more military action to protect global trade and its own interests.
The U.S. broke the ceasefire with new strikes and is not negotiating fairly. A deal must lift the naval blockade completely.
The strait must reopen soon so oil can flow freely; otherwise, every country will feel the pain of higher prices.
